messages:
maria: FYI I ran an offline trace-driven replay to stress continuous batching choices. Used a 12h sampled production trace and toggled token_budget, max_batch and a short-hold queue policy. Observed a p95 regression in a subset of windows when max_batch >= 80 and token_budget >= 256.

kevin: Can you share the concrete numbers and which metric regressed? tail latency, throughput, or both? :eyes:

maria: Tail. Baseline heuristics (token_budget=128, max_batch=48, queue_timeout=20ms) -> p50 38ms p95 205ms TPS 420. Replay variant A (token_budget=256, max_batch=96, no short-hold) -> p50 40ms p95 360ms TPS 440. Throughput rises but tail spikes.

ash: Which kernels were picked in the high-tail windows? My suspicion: larger batch sizes triggered blocked/strided kernels that pay a penalty for mixed seq lengths and cause extra KV shuffles.

maria: I pulled the kernel selection histogram. During tail windows, blocked_attn_v2 usage rose from 12% -> 48%, generic_attn fell proportionally. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.78 -> 0.66 in the same windows. The profiler shows extra KV materialization time.

kevin: That KV hit drop is worrisome. Did the replay simulate cache capacity/eviction accurately?

maria: Yes, trace_replay honors kv_capacity and eviction policy flags. Command I used: 
```
./trace_replay --trace=prod_sample_12h.log \
  --token-budget=256 --max-batch=96 --queue-timeout-ms=15 \
  --kv-capacity=1GB --kv-evict=LRU --seed=2026 \
  --record=run_256_96
```

maria: Example perf row from the run: 
```
req: 0x9b2f
kernel: blocked_attn_v2
kv_hit: 0.64
decode_toks: 240
latency_ms: 378
```

natalie: Two experiment ideas: (1) seq_len bucketing: bias batch formation to group by prefix-length buckets, (2) short-hold policy: hold short requests for up to bucket_age_ms to increase homogeneity. Run A/B: current heuristics vs bucket+short-hold with token_budget=128.

ash: Agreed. Also test a token_budget floor per-request (e.g., clamp to min(remaining_budget, 64)) to avoid huge budgets encouraging oversized batches.

maria: I'll run an A/B in the eval harness. Plan: run trace_replay A (current) vs B (seq-bucket + short-hold, token_budget=128, max_batch=64). Collect per-window kernel hist, kv_hit over time, p50/p95/TPS, and decode token distribution. 24h replay each, sample 10% to keep runtime feasible.

dev-bot: CI: started replay A -> artifacts: s3://redwood-replays/1742001234/runA/summary.json
dev-bot: CI: started replay B -> artifacts: s3://redwood-replays/1742001234/runB/summary.json

maria: Assigned to me to run, collate diffs, and post a short findings doc. If B reduces p95 by >=30ms without quality regression and keeps TPS +/-5%, we can push a canary of short-hold + seq-bucket to Dedicated behind a runtime flag.

kevin: Please include rollback criteria and a small prompt-regression smoke suite in the evaluation so we don't miss subtle quality differences.

natalie: I'll wire dashboard panels for kernel% breakdown and kv_hit time series for the run IDs. Add me to the artifact ACLs.

maria: Done. Kicking off the A/B now with the commands and will share the summary once both finish. Thanks all. :rocket:
